name: Republic of Cuba

places.name: San Antonio de los Banos air base

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 109,884 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 103,800 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes Isla de la Juventud; the US Guantanamo Bay leased area is inside the island.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 10,937,203). Low/high +/-3% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:CUB. Official/UN figures may overstate the resident population after the 2021-2024 emigration wave.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 p.427 as quoted: 49,000 active (excludes 26,500 paramilitary). CIA Factbook 2025: ~50,000 (limited information).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2024: 39,000 ready reserves (serve 45 days a year). The 1,120,000 reserve paramilitary (Territorial Troops Militia etc.) is not counted; high adds an educated share of its trained core.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 49,000 (IISS 2024) minus infantry P roles (8,000 + 12,000). Covers navy (~3,000), air and air-defence force (~8,000), armour/artillery crews, logistics and staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Cuba's own "War of All the People" doctrine: the Territorial Troops Militia, Youth Labour Army and Civil Defence reserve total ~1,120,000 (IISS as quoted), ~10% of population. Educated judgement on what could be armed.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5: experienced Soviet-trained officer corps (Angola, Ethiopia 1975-91), now aging; 32 Cuban military/intelligence personnel died guarding Maduro in Jan 2026, showing an active security role abroad.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: revolutionary identity and political control (MININT/FAR integration).

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75 for home defence against the US ("War of All the People"); economic crisis, blackouts and emigration depress the low bound.

weapons.note: Anchor 8 plus: Soviet 1970s guided weapons (Malyutka, Strela, Styx), no precision strike.

ships.note: Anchor 8: converted trawlers, Osa/Pauk craft, midget submarine.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: extensive tunnel and shelter network built for the War of All the People, coastal defence sites; SAM belt around Havana.

logistics.note: Anchor 8: rail (8,367 km) and trucks, acute fuel shortage.

communications.note: Anchor 8-9: Soviet-era radio, Chinese/Russian assistance (Bejucal SIGINT site).

isr.note: Anchor 8-9: legacy radars, Chinese-linked SIGINT stations (reported); no satellites or UAV fleet.

cyber.note: Below anchor 9-10: state internet control (ETECSA), intelligence-led cyber activity.

gdpPerCapita.note: GDP below / population 10,937,203. The Factbook per-capita line ($23,700, 2024) is inconsistent with its own GDP and population and is not used.

gdp.note: World Bank has no PPP GDP for Cuba and the IMF does not cover it. CIA Factbook real GDP PPP 2024 $81.165 bn (2015 dollars, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/central-america-n-caribbean/cu.json) x US GDP deflator 2011/2015 (FRED GDPDEF 91.478/97.315 = 0.940, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=GDPDEF&fq=Annual) = 76.3 bn 2011 int$. Range +/-25% (no PPP benchmark for Cuba; 2025 contraction during the energy crisis).

milSpendShare.note: CIA Factbook: 4.2% of GDP (2020), 3.2% (2019); SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS 2.88% (2018, last value) low. Opaque budget; mid an educated middle.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2024: industry incl. construction 23.85% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS).

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.78. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/CUB/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 15.53% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.69 (mean 2017-2019, range 0.68-0.72). Mid 1 - 0.155/0.69 = 0.78. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.68 = 0.7. High: s 0.72 = 0.78. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 69% of domestic calorie supply. FAO balance sheets for Cuba stop at 2019; the post-2020 output collapse is not in s, so the true value is likely lower. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports most of its food (rice, wheat, chicken); rationing in place; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 5,393,966 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.554% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 59,916. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-15%.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. No road figure on the fetched Factbook record or the road-network table; older Factbook editions gave ~60,000 km total with roughly 20,000 km paved (2015). Mid is the derived midpoint.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook 8,367 km (2017; 8,195 km standard gauge, incl. sugar-industry lines); World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM 5,076 km (2007) low.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 34 ports, 6 large + 3 medium = 9 (Havana, Mariel, Cienfuegos, Santiago de Cuba, Nuevitas, Matanzas...).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Cuba is below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-fleet table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country); CIA Factbook 2023 counts 65 merchant ships (13 general cargo, 10 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Island defence on interior lines; fuel shortage limits motorized movement.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (~900,000) and draught oxen widely used in agriculture since the 1990s Special Period; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Cuba is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Party to the NPT since 2002 and Tlatelolco; no Russian nuclear weapons stationed since 1962.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: island fortified with tunnels and militia, population mobilization doctrine; high 1.3 for the tropical climate and dense organised resistance.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2024-25 data with 2026 order of battle. Most data are IISS estimates (Military Balance 2024 personnel, 2025 equipment via the List of equipment of the Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces) with many "n/a" quantities, so counts are grade C/D and heavily storage-inflated; serviceability is very low. Population convention: everything inside ne:CUB (World Bank). GDP from CIA Factbook (World Bank/IMF give no PPP series), rebased to 2011 int$ via FRED GDPDEF; grade C. ships_minor = patrol ships, missile craft, MCM; missiles = coastal anti-ship launchers. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Territorial Troops Militia and Youth Labour Army (~1.12 million reserve paramilitary) excluded from active and P roles; they feed mobilizable.
